chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from ʿAli ibn Ri'ab, from Abi Basir, who said:
I asked Aba Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who killed an insane man, and he said:

“If the insane man had attacked him and he defended himself, then killed him, there is nothing against him in retaliation nor blood-money, and his heirs are to be given the blood-money from the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims.”

He said: “But if he killed him without the insane man having attacked him, then there is no retaliation for one from whom retaliation is not taken; and I hold that the blood-money is upon his killer, from his own property, which he pays to the heirs of the insane man, and he seeks forgiveness from Allah and repents to Him.”

key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims from which compensation may be paid
key_terms.دِيَةٍ: blood-money; financial compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.قَوَدٍ: retaliatory execution or legal retribution for killing
key_terms.مَجْنُونًا: an insane person; the legal subject discussed in the ruling
key_terms.وَرَثَتُهُ: his heirs, who are entitled to receive the blood-money
key_terms.يَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ: he repents to Him, meaning to Allah
key_terms.يَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ: he seeks Allah’s forgiveness for the wrongful act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone kills an insane person in self-defense or without being attacked?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal ruling for killing an insane person, distinguishing between self-defense and unjustified killing. If the killing occurred in self-defense, there is no retaliation or personal liability for blood-money, while the victim's heirs receive compensation from the public treasury; otherwise, the killer must pay the blood-money from his own wealth and repent to Allah.
